summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of bronchopulmonary dysplasia, tracheobronchomalacia, and tracheostomy dependence was admitted for low-grade fever, cough, and sore throat. She was diagnosed with acute tracheitis and started on Augmentin, which she tolerated well despite a documented penicillin allergy involving nausea and vomiting. A chest X-ray showed no pneumonia or other acute findings. Her symptoms improved during the hospital stay, and she was weaned off oxycodone for throat pain. Laboratory values, including potassium, normalized. She was discharged home on day three with instructions to complete a full course of Augmentin, resume her weekly Trulicity, and follow up with interventional pulmonology. All home medications were continued, and she was in stable condition at discharge.
